agencies.agency: City of Jacksonville — Office of Special Events
agencies.status_now: When we checked on Oct 25 the page said "No Upcoming Vending Opportunities". Applications open event by event (Holiday River Fest, World of Nations, Jazz Fest and more).
agencies.fees_text: Set per event, typically 15% of gross sales. For non-food-truck vendors the fee includes a tent, two tables, two chairs and a banner. Paid by cashier's check or money order to the City of Jacksonville. No refunds.
agencies.insurance_text: Food vendors send a certificate of insurance within 14 days of being accepted (City general insurance requirements).
agencies.food_text: Food vendors: Florida DBPR temporary event license (sold on site) and a JFRD fire inspection permit.
steps: Open the Become a Vendor page and check "Current Vending Opportunities".
Tap "receive vending opportunity updates" so you hear when an event opens.
When your event opens, fill in its application during the application window.
If accepted, have your sales tax certificate and business tax receipt ready, plus insurance if the event asks.
Pay the vendor fee the way the city asks (cashier's check or money order).

agencies.agency: Downtown Vision (DVI) — First Wednesday Art Walk
agencies.status_now: Art Walk runs the first Wednesday of every month, 5-9 PM, downtown. Applications are reviewed monthly; expect a reply after the first Wednesday.
agencies.food_text: Food trucks use a separate food truck application on the Art Walk page.
steps: Open the Art Walk artist/vendor application.
Fill in your business, products and photos.
Wait for a reply (they answer after each first Wednesday).
Bring your own power if you need it; outlets are not promised.

agencies.signup_label: How to vend at Seawalk Pavilion festivals
agencies.status_now: Festivals at the Seawalk Pavilion are run by outside producers; the city points vendors to each event producer's page.
steps: Open the city's Seawalk vendor FAQ and find the event you want.
Follow the link to that event's producer and apply there.
For the Opening of the Beaches Parade or other beach events, call Parks & Recreation for the application.

agencies.agency: City of Atlantic Beach — Farmers Market (with Dig Local Network)
agencies.signup_label: Atlantic Beach Farmers Market vendor application
agencies.status_now: Weekly on Sundays. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis; you list each item you plan to sell with photos.
steps: Open the Dig Local vendor application and pick "Atlantic Beach Farmers Market".
List each product with its price range and two photos.
Wait for approval; new items later need approval by email.

agencies.agency: City of St. Augustine Beach — City Events
agencies.status_now: Open now for the 7th Annual Beach Art Walk (Sat Nov 28, 1-6 PM) at Pier Park. The 7th Annual Holiday Market is Sat Dec 12, 3-7 PM.
agencies.fees_text: $45 per 10x10 booth (extra booths $45 each). Non-refundable. Your space is not reserved until you pay.
steps: Open the city's Vendor/Events Application.
Pick the event, add your contact info, number of tables and a link to your products.
Wait for the city to confirm, then pay the $45 booth fee (your spot is held only after payment).
Bring your own 10x10 setup; electricity is not provided.

agencies.agency: City of St. Augustine — Mobile Vendor / Business Permits
agencies.status_now: Selling on city streets needs a mobile vendor permit, applied for in person. Vending is restricted in some areas during Nights of Lights (Nov 21, 2026 - Jan 18, 2027).
steps: Read the Mobile Vendor page and the map of prohibited areas.
Fill in the mobile vendor application.
Turn it in in person at 151 King Street (call first).
For a booth at a festival, apply to that event's organizer instead.

agencies.signup_label: St. Johns County Parks & Rec events and permits

steps: Open the Parks & Recreation page and go to "Event Permits and Applications".
Email or call Parks & Rec to ask which county events are taking vendors.
Apply the way they tell you for that event.

Ask Parks & Recreation how to join a city event as a vendor.

extra_links: City special events + itinerant merchant form
steps: For First Friday: open the First Fridays page and use the vendor link, or contact Surf 97.3.
For other events: fill in the special event application and the itinerant merchant application.
Send forms and proof of insurance to the Deputy City Clerk (address on the city page).

common_permits.name: Florida sales tax registration + Annual Resale Certificate
common_permits.detail: Register with the Florida Department of Revenue to collect sales tax; registered businesses get an Annual Resale Certificate. Many events ask for your certificate number.

common_permits.name: Local business tax receipt (LBTR)
common_permits.detail: Get it from the tax collector in the county where your business is based. In Duval, receipts run Oct 1 - Sep 30; late renewals add 10% in October plus 5% a month (max 25%).

common_permits.name: Certificate of insurance (COI)
common_permits.who: When the event or city asks
common_permits.detail: Some events ask for general liability insurance naming them as additional insured. The City of Jacksonville wants food vendors' COI within 14 days of acceptance.

common_permits.name: Temporary food event license (DBPR)
common_permits.detail: Food vendors without an annual license need a temporary event license from Florida DBPR; it is not needed for jewelry, art or other merchandise.
